title: The Cause of Chocolate’s Rampage
text: “Boo-boo-boo!? Oink? Boo-oink!?”
Hearing the commotion, a pair of pigs came out of the house.
“You lot! The ones watching me have finally come to attack! You said it was all in my head, but look now, was I not right!”
Watching him? Surely he meant that Rafumi knew about her own past. Though it seemed he’d believed he was being watched for quite a while now.
“B-Boo-hahahaha-hyahyahya!? Boo-hya!”
Somehow there was laughter mixed in with the screaming.
“Motoyasu-sama, is that person startled or laughing? Which is it?”
Yuki-chan seemed to have noticed the same thing.
“Boo… Hahah!”

The pig sounded like it was doing an impression of some famous amusement-park mascot’s laugh, indeed. Then it noticed the bandit and raised its voice even louder. Something about “Big Brother!” it seemed to be saying.
“Hmph!? You… how dare you show your face before me so brazenly! I won’t forgive this kind of insolence!”
“Mmm——”
The bandit let out a groan as though reuniting with some detestable enemy, turning its face away. Parent and child alike appeared to be thoroughly captured by Rafumi.
“Hmph! It’s the mediocre son from next door! Hurry up and help me get rid of this intruder! This is a thief who’s come to steal the genius’s research products!”
The bandit’s parent seemed to be barking orders at Ren’s companion leader.
“…Still the same as ever, huh… still going on about conspiracies.”
Ren’s companion leader let out a heavy sigh, muttering under his breath while casting a sympathetic glance at the bandit.

“Honestly… to not even realize how thoroughly you’ve been neutralized, how foolish can you possibly be. Right… it was around the time your parent died that your true nature showed itself. Clinging to some tiny taste of success, you make bizarre chocolates and force them on everyone around you, fishing for praise. Even if your soul isn’t rotten, your character certainly is, through and through.”

There was an unusual note of anger mixed into Rafumi’s normally flat tone, I say. Father had once mentioned something about the bandit’s parent. Apparently there are men past a certain age who go on endlessly bragging about their elementary school glory days. It’s a problem when someone can only talk about childhood achievements, or so the theory went. Surely things happened in middle school and high school too — so what did it mean that this man could only ever talk about elementary school?

“For me, it’s a dream come true that someone like you can be dealt with so swiftly. You’ll have to pay with your own body for turning chocolate into a toy, won’t you? After all, you yourself are one of the reasons chocolate goes berserk around here every single year.”
“Eh!? What!? Hold on a moment please. S-so that’s how it was!?”
When Ren’s companion leader cried out, Rafumi turned around.

“Of course, that’s one reason, but not the only one. The main cause is those who defile love itself by playing games with chocolate. It’s not just this one fool. Everyone in this world is at fault. Love is a great and precious thing, you know.”

Rafumi, aren’t you the one who actually hates the world? I want to help Father, who hates the world — but someone like you, who also hates the world, means nothing to me, indeed. No, wait — if you’re going to become a Demon Lord, then I’d rather finish you off as a proper Hero should.
“Shall I finish you off here and now?”

“What? Are you still sore about the time I attacked Shield Hero? I did have some feelings about the matter of Shield Hero’s little tampering with the chocolate, but I wouldn’t go that far over something so trivial. It wasn’t done of my own will, though I admit it went too far.”
“What did Father do, exactly?”
“Ah, that. Keel and Fi… no, better I not say, since you’d only be delighted to hear it.”
She wasn’t even being properly suggestive about it, I say.
“What do you know!? Tell me!”

What did Father do to the chocolate? What could possibly make me happy about it? Was it the Valentine’s sweets Father made for everyone in the village each year? All I remember is that they tasted perfectly normal and delicious.
“What Shield Hero slipped into the chocolate was……”
“What Father slipped in was……?”
I recognized this pattern all too well.
“That would be Filo’s… fufu, wouldn’t it be far more amusing to leave it hanging right here without explaining? I won’t tell you! Chan!”
That Rafumi! She did the exact same thing to me that she did to Ren! Blast it! What did Father do that involved Filo-tan!
“Tell me properly, I say!”
“Oh my, shouldn’t you be more worried about what’s behind you, Spear Hero?”
“What is it—— Hyii!?”
Something ominous was drifting off of Yuki-chan.

“W-what’s wrong, Yuki-chan? You mustn’t pay any mind to Rafumi’s nonsense. I was simply pressing Father about what he put into the chocolate concerning Filo-tan… purely so he doesn’t make the same mistake twice in the future.”
I spoke with as stern an expression as I could manage, trying to dispel whatever aura was pouring off of Yuki-chan.
“Yuki-chan. I’ll treasure and eat every bit of the chocolate you made for me. Let’s make some together next time.”
“Motoyasu-sama…… understood!”

Phew, indeed. A promise to make chocolate together with Yuki-chan. Making it together ought to be safe enough. Now that I think of it, pigs are notorious for mixing the strangest things into their chocolate. Blood, hair, fingernails — those are the cute cases. Sometimes something like actual poison ends up mixed in, and people faint from it. Some Filolial-samas are skilled cooks, but plenty are hopeless at it too. So making chocolate together is simply the safer route, I say.

“Enough about Spear Hero for now…… Back then I foolishly stumbled into a trap and made a pathetic spectacle of myself, but I am not the same now. If you’re so desperate to shock everyone around you with chocolate, allow me to show you how it’s properly done.”
Having redirected my attention toward Yuki-chan, Rafumi puffed up her tail and pressed a finger to the bandit parent’s forehead.
“Guh!? You— wh-what are you— Agagaga, Gyaaaa!? S-stop, please, aaah, my— my backside! N-noooo, chocolaaaaate! Chocooooo! Agaaa——”

The bandit’s parent let out some incomprehensible shriek, eyes rolled back white. Before long, he went limp and lost consciousness entirely. He must have been shown some truly horrifying vision, indeed.
“Now this fool’s own precious invention will torment him with nightmares, casting himself as the test subject…… until he can’t so much as look at chocolate ever again, hm? Raf-raf-raf!”
“Aaaaah……”
“Boo-hyaaaa……”
“Mmmm——”
The bandit, both pigs, and Ren’s companion leader all trembled, staring at Rafumi.

“Raf-raf-raf! Retribution for those who dare play with chocolate! I understand all too well the feelings Shield Hero must have had toward this man! If this doesn’t teach him his lesson…… then it’ll be chocolate again next time! Since I couldn’t unleash it on Black Thunder, I’ve vented it all on you instead!”

And so Rafumi’s triumphant laughter rang out across the land. Afterward, the incident came to be known in that region as the “Chocolate’s Revenge,” and it seems the lesson taken from it wasn’t merely “don’t play with your food” but rather a strict rule that chocolate must be handled with the utmost care, lest it pass judgment upon you. Incidentally, the “feelings” Father supposedly had were apparently nothing more than a stern lecture. When I reported the whole affair to Father afterward, he remarked that between Black Thunder and now this, Ren really did seem to have a lot going on with chocolate.

A few days had passed since Rafumi wreaked havoc at the chocolate farm. The bandit’s parent had been reduced to a shell of himself and was set to convalesce for some time, while the bandit himself was apparently ordered to work at the family estate. In the meantime, Ren’s companion leader had proposed to Rafumi that he eventually be brought along on adventures as a hero’s collaborator, to which Rafumi had responded with something along the lines of generous consideration. And so…… the circus’s next destination happened to be the town right next to Riska’s hometown.
